text:
Dawn at the Orrin Flats comes without ceremony: a long grey horizon, a wind that carries salt from somewhere unseen, and a concrete guideway running 48 kilometres into nothing. On 14 March 2031, the final acceleration trial began here in that same quiet.

The Vantry Transit Authority had spent years working toward the day. Dr. Selwyn Marachek, chief test engineer, oversaw the run from the control building and later confirmed the reading himself. The prototype reached 540 km/h and held it for 38 seconds across a 21 km stretch of the guideway.

The figure appears in Trial Report VTA-MX-17, released after independent verification of both the onboard and trackside speed logs. It stands as the top speed recorded by the Vantry maglev prototype, a number now settled on paper, though the flats themselves seem unchanged.
